key_insight: A neural network potential trained on first-principles data can accurately capture oxygen-vacancy formation and long-time diffusion in SrTiO3 at scales that are impractical for direct ab initio molecular dynamics.
engineering_relevance: This enables more reliable prediction of defect-driven transport in perovskite oxides, supporting design of oxide electronics, ionic conductors, and related functional materials.
method: Generate AIMD/DFT reference data for pristine and oxygen-deficient SrTiO3.
Train a neural network potential to reproduce energies, forces, and virials.
Run large-scale, long-time NNP molecular dynamics to compute vacancy diffusion and Arrhenius migration enthalpy.
evidence_signal: The NNP matches DFT energies, forces, virials, and vacancy formation energies across supercell sizes, and its diffusion results agree better with experiment, including a 0.64 eV migration enthalpy versus the 0.67 eV experimental value.
watch_item: Accuracy depends on the quality and coverage of the DFT training set, so unusual defect configurations or extreme conditions may require additional reference data before deployment.
paper_title: Theoretical Investigation of Oxygen-Vacancy Diffusion in SrTiO$_3$ using Neural Network Potentials
